thread_analysis.thread_summary: NEC Platforms / Google Fluoride Host Stack registration attempt, run via Allion as registration agent. All tested Fluoride versions (1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6) produced the same fatal GAP-GATT ICS Consistency Check Invalid findings (GATT 7/5 or 7/6 Supported requiring GAP 25/5,35/5 or 25/6,35/6; and related GATT 4/25 mandatory findings), which blocks Design Number registration regardless of which module/Controller QDID is paired with it. GAP/GATT are Host-layer issues, so changing the Controller QDID does not help. The customer also needed guidance on verifying their SIG Launchstudio account and company association, and on the invoice/payment process for the registration fee.
all_questions_found: Which Google Fluoride version is safe for Bluetooth certification?
Is Google Fluoride 1.6 compatible with our module, given that 1.4 and 1.5 both failed?
Can the GAP-GATT Consistency Check error be fixed by switching the Controller or module QDID, or does the module need to satisfy specific GAP requirements?
How do we verify our SIG Launchstudio account and company association (i.e., which company/email the logged-in account is registered under)?
How do we obtain the SIG registration fee Invoice to proceed with payment (which account should be used to log in and generate it)?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Google Fluoride 1.3/1.4/1.5/1.6 all share the same internal ICS defect: GATT items (7/5) and (7/6) being Supported require corresponding GAP items (25/5 or 35/5, and 25/6 or 35/6 respectively) to also be Supported, and GATT (1/2 and 4/15)/(4/16)/(4/22) being Supported require GATT (4/25) to be Mandatory — none of which Fluoride's ICS satisfies, producing fatal Invalid findings on the Consistency Check that block Design Number registration. GAP and GATT are both Host-layer (not Controller-layer) items — no amount of Controller/module QDID changes will resolve a Host-layer ICS inconsistency. The consultant speculated Bluetooth SIG added this ICS check rule after Fluoride was originally registered. The only solution is to use a compliant, already-registered Host Stack (e.g. BlueZ) or a future fixed Fluoride version.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: 1. Identify Fluoride as the Host Stack → flag immediately for GAP-GATT inconsistency risk. 2. GAP/GATT error → Host Stack problem → must change Host Stack. 3. Controller/module QDID is irrelevant to this error.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Proceeding with Fluoride wastes test and registration fees and blocks product launch. Advising a module change instead of Host Stack change wastes engineering resources.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Any project using Google Fluoride must be flagged at intake for the known GAP-GATT Consistency Check blocker. Escalate immediately to inform the customer that DN registration is blocked until they switch Host Stack or SIG verifies a fixed Fluoride release.
